sections.h2: Where is Ballard County and how did it start?
sections.html:
Ballard County fills the far western tip of Kentucky where the Ohio River meets the Mississippi, in the Jackson Purchase. The county's own site calls it the ninety-third county formed, established February 15, 1842, from parts of Hickman and McCracken, and says it covers 254 square miles. Wikipedia's Census-based total is 274 square miles, including 27 of water.

The first seat was Blandville. A courthouse fire on February 17, 1880 burned most early records, and Wickliffe took over as seat in 1882. Anyone tracing an old parcel should ask the County Clerk what survives for the years before 1880.

sections.h2: Which towns and neighborhoods share the same tax offices?
sections.html:
Barlow, Kevil, La Center and Wickliffe are the four cities, and La Center is the largest. Bandana and Lovelaceville are census-designated places. All of the 2020 population was classed as rural, and a single school system, Ballard County Schools, covers the county. Axe Lake Swamp State Nature Preserve, 458 acres in the Barlow Bottoms, is part of a 3,000-acre wetland complex.

Water marks three sides of the county. Across the Ohio River sit Pulaski and Alexander counties in Illinois, and across the Mississippi sits Mississippi County, Missouri. McCracken County, home to the Paducah area, borders Ballard on the east and Carlisle County on the south, and the county belongs to the Paducah, Kentucky and Illinois metropolitan area.

Every one of these places pays through the same three courthouse-area offices:

  • Sheriff, 437 Ohio Street, Wickliffe: bills and payments, (270) 335-3561 or (270) 335-5153.
  • Property Valuation Administrator, 132 North 4th Street, Wickliffe: assessments and exemptions, (270) 335-3400.
  • County Clerk, 132 North 4th Street, Wickliffe: appeals and, later, unpaid bills, (270) 335-5168.

sections.h2: Is Ballard County growing or shrinking?
sections.html:
It is shrinking slowly. The population peaked at 14,378 in 1880, fell 41.6 percent to 8,390 by 1890, stayed between 7,900 and 8,800 from 1950 through 2010. By 2020 the count had slipped 6.3 percent to 7,728, and the 2025 estimate is lower again at 7,594. The 2020 census found 3,228 households, 29.3 percent of them one person living alone and 14.8 percent a person 65 or older living alone.

A seller with a tax lien should clear it before listing so that title work does not hold up a closing.

sections.h2: When does a Ballard County bill become late?
sections.html:
One statewide rhythm, written into KRS 134.015, governs Ballard County bills unless the state approves a delay. Settle the whole bill by November 1 for a 2 percent reduction. From November 2 until year end the printed total is due. A January payment draws 5 percent extra, and a later one draws 10 percent.

Kentucky's revenue agency describes what comes next. Bills still open at closing time on April 15 go to the County Clerk as certificates of delinquency, and a lien is recorded against the property. Monthly interest of 1 percent begins, with clerk and county attorney fees after it. If a delayed schedule is ever used, each stage becomes a one-month window, so check the dates printed on the bill with the sheriff's office.

sections.h2: What happens each year from January to December?
sections.html:
The Kentucky property tax year as it applies to a Ballard County parcel
Month or windowWhat occurs
January 1Value date for real estate
January 1 to March 1Real property listing window
First Monday in May, 13 daysPublic inspection of the tax roll
Day after inspection endsLast day to file an appeal with the clerk
25 to 35 days laterLocal board hears appeals for up to five days
December 31Bills due without penalty

Owners need not list real estate again if last year's roll described it completely and correctly and nothing major changed. Buyers may treat the deed price as the listed value for the following January 1.

sections.h2: How does a Ballard County appeal work?
sections.html:
Start with a conference at the PVA, 132 North 4th Street, because state rules bar a filing without one. After that, the County Clerk accepts your appeal until closing time on the workday following the end of inspection. The form asks for your own opinion of value, and the bill uses it if the bill is printed before the case ends.

  • Evidence to bring: descriptions of the land and structures, insurance policies, construction costs, nearby sales listings.
  • Anyone paid to speak for you needs recognized credentials and your written authority.
  • You may audio-record the hearing.
  • A higher value set by the board produces a supplemental bill for the difference.

An owner who never files with the local board, or files and then skips the hearing, cannot take the case to a later stage.

sections.h2: Do older residents in Ballard County get a discount?
sections.html:
Kentucky's homestead exemption is claimed through the Ballard County PVA by owners who are 65 or older or classified as totally disabled. It takes $49,100 off assessed value for 2025 and 2026 and is reset every second year. Many residents could qualify: 21.4 percent of residents were 65 or older in 2020, the median age was 44.8, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate of 7,594 people is 1.8 percent below its April 2020 base.

An owner who never applied might be paying tax on value the state would exempt. A call to the PVA at (270) 335-3400 settles it.

Retail sales were $56.7 million in 2022, about $7,415 per resident, and accommodation and food sales were $3.3 million. Among adults, 93.9 percent finished high school and 18.4 percent hold a bachelor's degree or more. Computers are in 95.0 percent of households and broadband in 87.6 percent, which helps owners who want to research a parcel or an appeal online.

sections.h2: What does a Ballard County house cost, and who lives in them?
sections.html:
The 2020 to 2024 survey puts the middle owner-occupied home at $145,800, with owners living in 76.0 percent of occupied homes. Typical gross rent was $817 and income at the middle was $66,164. The county had 3,209 households and 3,730 housing units in 2025. The 2020 count put the vacancy rate at 12.4 percent of units and a rental vacancy rate of 12.0 percent.

Jobs are small in number: 155 employer establishments with 1,617 workers in 2023, up 19.2 percent in a year, and $87.0 million in payroll. The typical commute is 26.5 minutes. About 15.9 percent of residents are in poverty and 354 are veterans.

sections.h2: How do taxes work when a Ballard County house is sold?
sections.html:
Kentucky law makes the tax the owner's personal debt as of the assessment date, and a recorded delinquency lien can ride with the land for up to eleven years under any owner. For that reason the closing agent usually pays the year's bill from the seller's proceeds. Ask how the year will be split with the buyer.

  • Ask the sheriff for current and past-due amounts.
  • Ask the clerk whether a lien is recorded.
  • Put a mailing address for the next bill in the deed, as KRS 382.135 requires.

If you inherited a river-county house or moved away and now owe back taxes, you can request a written cash offer. A lien balance comes out of the price at closing.

faqs.q: Who do I pay in Ballard County?
faqs.a: Pay the Sheriff at 437 Ohio Street, Wickliffe. The county's page for elected offices lists (270) 335-3561 and (270) 335-5153.

faqs.q: How much do I save by paying early?
faqs.a: Two percent of the bill, provided the sheriff has the full amount by November 1 (KRS 134.015). After that date the printed amount stands through December 31.
The bill picks up 5 percent in January and 10 percent afterward. Once April 15 passes, the County Clerk holds it and interest of 1 percent a month runs.

faqs.q: Where is an assessment appeal filed?
faqs.a: File with the County Clerk, 132 North 4th Street, after your PVA conference. Filing closes the workday after inspection ends.

faqs.q: Is the homestead exemption a county program?
faqs.a: No, the state runs it. The Ballard County PVA, (270) 335-3400, takes applications from owners 65 or older or totally disabled, and the 2025 and 2026 amount is $49,100.
